messages.subject: add latent variables
parts:
in my model, WDI is- the only latent variable- calculated by summation of (dams + ditch + aqueduct) then standardized the results to have WDI in new data column. 
so, when I built the model, how couldI insert WDI as latent variable; 
shouldn't I use the calculated WDI?
WDI =~ dams + ditch + aqueduc
or should I remove calculated WDI column and insert WDI in specific equation 
WDI =~ dams + ditch + aqueduc 

library(lavaan)
model <- '
# measurement model (latent variables)
WDI =~ dams + ditch + aqueduct

# regressions
ln.intro ~ WDI+asn.dev+ln.area+sqr.diversity
sqr.impact ~ ln.intro+WDI+asn.dev+sqr.diversity
sqr.diversity ~ ln.area

# residual correlations
WDI ~~ asn.dev 
WDI ~~ ln.area 
asn.dev ~~ ln.area'

fit.light <- sem(model, data = light)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: add latent variables
parts:
in my model, WDI is- the only latent variable- calculated by summation of (dams + ditch + aqueduct) then standardized the results to have WDI in new data column. 
so, when I built the model, how couldI insert WDI as latent variable; 
shouldn't I use the calculated WDI?
WDI =~ dams + ditch + aqueduc
or should I remove calculated WDI column and insert WDI in specific equation 
WDI =~ dams + ditch + aqueduc

A sum score does not remove measurement error, it only reduces the proportion of measurement error (relative to the proportion in dams, ditch, and aqueduc).  Defining a latent variable with the same observed measures should remove measurement error (if the assumption of a common underlying cause is true).

I believe specifying "WDI =~ dams + ditch + aqueduc" in your model syntax will define a latent variable "WDI" and ignore the observed variable of the same name, but it would be better to avoid confusion by deleting the sum score or by changing the name of the latent variable, e.g., "WDI.factor =~ dams + ditch + aqueduc"

Terry
